notes: TBox rule edit: every mechanical wave can travel through a vacuum. Derivability very_unlikely: needing a material medium is what defines a mechanical wave (Wikipedia), stated in general form in teaching texts ("mechanical waves need a medium" 89, "mechanical wave" 26,235). Counterfactual: clearly false, and a common student confusion of mechanical with electromagnetic waves. It edits a definition rather than a contingent class rule, as most TBox rules in this topic do. The paraphrase has the same polarity as the direct question (both "no" before the edit). Derived queries name made-up wave kinds (Halvorsen ripple, Teague wave, Ardell wave) known only by their class (inheritance, 2 hops): can a Halvorsen ripple cross a vacuum, can a Teague wave carry a signal between spacecraft (application), and does an Ardell wave need a medium (yes before, no after). Sound is not used, since its need for a medium is stored by name. The negation is worded "some mechanical wave cannot ...". The near query asks which medium sound crosses fastest (steel).
